newsitem.title: USA: Bema near deal on Cerro Casale project.
newsitem.headline: Bema near deal on Cerro Casale project.

text.p: Bema Gold Corp expects to sell its 33 percent stake on Arizona Star Resources Corp within the next three months, bringing a partner into the company's $1 billion Cerro Casale project in Chile, said John Anderson, Bema's director of investor relations.
The Cerro Casale project contains an estimated 24.8 million ounces of gold and 6.4 billion pounds of copper and is 49 percent owned by Bema and 51 percent owned by Arizona Star, Anderson said.
Bema said it has confidentiality agreements with 20 companies regarding development of the property and one of the company's tests were comparable to Bema's earlier forecasts, Anderson said.
Bema is seeking a major mining company to help build the mine, arrange financing and help in production, Anderson said.
The Cerro Casale project is expected to produce 800,000 ounces of gold annually and 250 million pounds of copper per year, Anderson said.
Factoring in the sale of copper, Bema's operating costs of mining are expected to be $100 per ounce of gold, Anderson said.
Proceeds from the sale of Arizona Star will be used to develop Bema's Quebrada, Cerro Roman and Venezuelan properties, Anderson said.
